chapters.title: Twenty-five years of friendship
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: two six-year-old girls at a school desk on the first day of school, one holding a pencil, the other an apple, both laughing, big backpacks, sunny classroom

chapters.title: Drifting apart
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 2 SCENE: two young men standing on two different train platforms, waving to each other as the trains pull away in opposite directions, soft evening light, a little sad but warm

chapters.title: Arguments and making up
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 3 SCENE: a small shared kitchen, one red-haired bearded man cooking at the stove and his flatmate washing dishes at the sink, both smiling, a little chart on the fridge drawn as simple icons

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is friendship. Leyla, how did you meet your best friend?
On the first day of school. We were six. She took my pencil, and I took her apple.
[laugh] A fair trade.
We hit it off immediately. Twenty-five years later, she's still my best friend. But now she lives in Canada.
Oh, so it's a long-distance friendship.
Yes. There's a nine-hour time difference. When I wake up, she's going to bed.
How do you keep it strong?
Every Sunday morning we have a video call. Sometimes it's two hours. And she always remembers my exams, my interviews, everything. She's so supportive.
That's loyalty. I'm a bit jealous. I had a best friend at school too — Danny. But after university we started to drift apart.
What happened?
Nothing big. No conflict, no fight. He moved to another city, got married, and we just… stopped calling.
[sigh] That happens to many people. It's sad, but it's normal.
Last month I sent him a message. We talked for an hour, like in the old days.
That's lovely! And do you and your friends ever argue?
Of course. My flatmate and I argue about the dishes every week.
[chuckle] And then you make up?
Always. We found a compromise — I cook, and he washes up.
For me, the most important thing is trust. I can tell my friend anything, and it stays between us.
Agreed. And a real friend will stand by someone even when they make a mistake.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: who is your oldest friend — and how did you meet?
Mine is Danny. I think I'll call him again. See you next time!
Bye for now!
